title: rootdens
intro:
Root density calculations.
  < component (SpRtLength 100 [m/g]) >

    SpRtLength: number [m/g]
     Parameter (default 100)
     Specific root length

sections.name: Anders Pedersen
sections.desc:
Use exponential function for root density. In this variant of Gerwitz and Page, ’a’
is specified as a function of development stage. See also [Gerwitz and Page, 1974]
sections.sig:
< "Anders Pedersen" (a DS a DS )
                               (q q )
                               ;; Shared parameters are described in chapter 73.
                               (SpRtLength 100 [m/g]) >

attrs.name: a DS
attrs.doc: Form parameter as a function of development stage.

attrs.name: q
attrs.doc:
Extra root length below max rooting depth. Root density will decrease linearly
     from the GP calculated amount at max rooting depth to zero ’q’ further down.

sections.name: DS Depth
sections.desc: Specify root density as a function of development stage.
sections.sig:
< DS Depth (entries entries ...)
                 ;; Shared parameters are described in chapter 73.
                 (SpRtLength 100 [m/g]) >

attrs.name: entries
attrs.doc:
A list of pairs, where the first element of each pair is a development stage
        (usually a number between 0 (emergence) and 2 (ripe), and the second element
        is a PLF specifying the relative root density as a function of soil depth in cm
        (a positive number).
        To find the absolute root density, Daisy will interpolate the relative root
        density distribution specified for the entries before and after the current de-
        velopment stage, and scale them to match the current total root mass.
           <    index density       >
           – index : number (dimension not specified)
             Parameter
             Index for specifying root density.
           – density: plf [<unknown> → <none>]
             Parameter
             Relative root density as a function of root depth .

sections.name: GP1D
sections.desc: Use exponential function for root density. See also [Gerwitz and Page, 1974]
sections.sig:
< GP1D (DensRtTip 0.1 [cm/cm3 ])
            (DensIgnore DensIgnore )
            ;; Shared parameters are described in chapter 73.
            (SpRtLength 100 [m/g]) >

attrs.name: DensIgnore
attrs.doc:
Ignore cells with less than this root density. By default, this is the same as
     DensRtTip.

attrs.name: k
attrs.doc:
Scale factor due to soil limit.
     Some roots might be below the soil imposed maximum root depth, or in areas
     with a density lower than the limit specified by DensIgnore. These roots will
     be re distributed within the root zone by multiplying the density with this
     scale factor.

sections.name: GP2D
sections.desc:
Use exponential function for root density in row crops.
    This is a two dimension model (z, x), where the z-axis is vertical, and the x-axis
is horizontal and ortogonal to the row. The row is assumed to be uniform (dense),
allowing us to ignore that dimension.
    We assume the root density decrease with horizontal distance to row, as well as
depth below row. See also [Gerwitz and Page, 1974]
sections.sig:
< GP2D        (DensRtTip 0.1 [cm/cm3 ])
                (DensIgnore DensIgnore )
                (debug 0)
                (row position 0 [cm])
                (row distance row distance )
                ;; Shared parameters are described in chapter 73.
                (SpRtLength 100 [m/g]) >

attrs.name: debug

attrs.name: MinDens
attrs.doc:
Minimal root density Root density will never be below this, as long as there is
    enough root mass. Extra root mass will be distributed according to Gerwitz
    and Page. If there are too little root mass, the root will have the same density
    all the way down.

sections.name: growth
sections.sig:
< growth (Depth Depth )
              (DensRtTip 0.1 [cm/cm3 ])
              (row position 0 [cm])

              (depth factor depth factor ) ; Has default value.
              (Width Width )

attrs.name: depth factor
attrs.doc:
Depth (negative) affect on root growth. Specify a value less than one to
    decrease root growth, and larger than one to increase root growth at the
    specified depth.

   row distance: number [cm]

attrs.name: depth factor
attrs.doc:
Depth (negative) affect on root growth. Specify a value less than one to
        decrease root growth, and larger than one to increase root growth at the
        specified depth.

attrs.name: neighbor effect
attrs.doc:
How fast root density in neighbor cells affect growth. After expansion, excess
        roots are distributed propertional to existing root desinity in each cell, plus a
        part of the neighbor cells.

attrs.name: max internal growth rate
attrs.doc: Root density within root zone cannot grow faster than this.

attrs.name: h threshold
attrs.doc: Root starts dying if pressure is above this threshold.

attrs.name: emerging
attrs.doc:
True until root mass is large enough to sustain root length in RZ. Until then,
    L within RZ is set to DensRtTip.

attrs.name: flooded
attrs.doc:
Time flooded, adjusted for temperature. The temperature adjustment is the
    same used for mineralization.
